utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody today. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you and good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, please, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. Daryl Mundis and Matthias Neuner for the Prosecution, assisted by our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to my colleagues from the Prosecution, everybody in the courtroom and around the courtroom. I'm Vasvija Vidovic, with Nicholas Robson, representing General Delic, with our legal assistant, Lejla Gluhic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. Just to put on the record that again we are -- the Chamber is sitting pursuant to Rule 15 bis. May the witness please be sworn in.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis. You may be seated, sir, and good morning to you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With regard to today's witness, I would first like to make a request for protective measures. Could we therefore please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If document PT2157 could be shown, please, now. I'm asking the usher to please, in the B/C/S, focus on the upper part of the document, by even enlarging the handwriting a little bit which is seen there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: PW-13, you see here in handwriting numbers "03" and "01". Could you explain what "03" and "01" stand for?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: The number "03" should stand for the third sector of the Military Security Service administration. "01" should stand for the first department of the Military Security Service administration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of the third department, the name standing behind "03"?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I assume that there was a full title. I cannot remember the name right now, but "03" referred to duties, and in our mutual communication, we used to say "the Analysis Sector."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name for Department 01?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: "01" was the Department for Counter-Intelligence Affairs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We see here in the handwriting that left of "03" and "01", the word "Izet" is written. Could you explain what "Izet" stands for?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: First, I'm trying to see if it's my handwriting here. I really cannot recognise if it's my handwriting. "Izet," that word is a name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us the full name of Izet, please?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: What I know is that in the Military Security Service Administration, there were at least two people with the name "Izet," so I really couldn't be sure here which one it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you look at the word "Vranduk" written below the "01", could you explain what "Vranduk" means?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: It's a secret name, code name, for operative processing or an operative action that was approved by the commander of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in reference to planned activities or activities that were supposed to be undertaken with the aim of more comprehensive observation of the Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain, if the word "Vranduk" is in handwriting on that document, where would that document go to within the Security Administration?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I didn't understand quite what you're asking. If I can ask you to clarify. From which point in time?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Vranduk" is in handwriting on this document. What significance do you attribute to this? What is the destiny of this document once "Vranduk" is written in handwriting on it?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Sir, I am not sure who put this word there, who wrote the word "Vranduk" here, but in principle I can say what I would do had I done that. I can say this in principle.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: When I received a document that, in my opinion, deserved attention and the approval of Vranduk procedures, I would entrust the chief of the first sector to carry out the activities that were planned, in accordance with his purview of duties. And then if I also happened to have some additional observations or requests of my own, then I would put that in my handwriting in the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what -- where would Section 1 in your office store that document?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: At the time, the control file of operations that were approved for processing were maintained by Izet Mustafic at the time. He was entrusted with maintaining this file.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned a name, Izet Mustafic. If you look at the document again and at the handwriting, we talked about "Izet" in the handwriting. Would you now maybe try to understand what "Izet" might refer to, the word "Izet" which is in handwriting on the document?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Had I written on the document, I would never have put it separately, away from where my number was. I would not put the name so far away from the number. So I'm just saying what I would do in principle. I would put it just underneath this number, "01".

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 956.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next document is Exhibit 364. This is a document from the, we can see, 21st of July. And if the usher exactly could again focus on the handwriting on the B/C/S. Thank you. Maybe make it a little bit smaller, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again, we see here "01" in handwriting on the document. Could you tell me what is meant by "01" here? Which section received the document?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: "01" is the Section for counter-intelligence affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do wait, Madam Vidovic, for the Registrar to say we're in open session before you go on to your next question.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you understand my question, Witness? If not, I can rephrase.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Just to make sure I understand you better, do you mean -- let's clarify this. Do you mean internal clashes? When you talk about clashes, do you mean internal clashes within the BH Army or within Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: There were sporadic internal clashes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You personally were involved in certain activities that were meant to deal with these problems; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown Exhibit 282.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we're waiting for the exhibit to come up, let me ask you this, Witness. You spoke to OTP investigators and you spoke in great detail about various operative actions, including Trebevic, Vranduk, Vasal, and so on and so forth; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you see in front of you is an order of the Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces, dated the 25th of October, 1993, and it's about the introduction of Trebevic and Trebevic-2 operations. Can you please look at the introduction to this order. You said you were involved in these Trebevic actions; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Instead of "involved," I would like to use the term "I was part of this." As far as I understand what you're saying, the year you mentioned is 1995, but the document patently shows the year 1993.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for that correction. I do accept this. But you were part of this action. Okay, I accept that. Could you please look at the introduction to this decision, and please comment based on your knowledge, since, as you suggest, you were part of this.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: As for the introduction, there's the header, some sort of a preamble to an order. I can't see who signed the --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we'll get to that. Let me ask you this: You agree that this order was based on a Presidency decision and on a joint order signed by the commander of the Supreme Command Staff of the Armed Forces and the Minister of the Interior; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were one of the participants in this event. You will agree that this was a joint activity by the Ministry of the Interior and the Supreme Command Staff of the Army; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we just look at the last page of this document, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do, and I think this was signed by General Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. We can put this document away now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just for my own clarification, Madam Vidovic, the witness -- Witness, you say you were a part of these operations, but I don't see your name on the list of people composing the groups. How were you part of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as far as I can tell, this is a general order from the highest possible level, the state level or, rather, the commander of the BH Army, and I think this order was followed by later orders in writing. Or in my specific case, I received a verbal order, for example, from my superior, my then superior, the chief of the Security Administration, to carry out a particular assignment that was part of this specific activity. If you want me to say what specific assignment, I'll be happy to share that with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we're getting to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not necessary to share it. Thank you so much I just wanted to understand that. Thank you. You may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we put this document away, please, and I want the witness to look at D738 now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have in front of you a record -- actually, it's a letter written on the 24th of November, 1993, containing minutes from the meeting of the President's Council for the Protection of the Constitutional Order, dated on 28th of October, 1993. And, Your Honours, if the witness could go straight to page 2 of the document, because it's very important. In the English, page two as well. Witness, what I want to ask you is this: You say you were part of these activities to do with the Trebevic action. Look at this portion just where it says "Agenda," and then further down from these minutes dated the 28th of October, minutes of the Presidency Council for the Protection of the Constitutional Order, held on the 28th of October, 1993: "This is a report on the operation conducted in order to implement the RBiH presidency decision with respect to relieving the commanders of the 10th Mountain Brigade and 9th Mountain [as interpreted] Brigade of their duties."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, perhaps I'll repeat. So this is -- my colleague is suggesting that it was recorded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you told us that you were involved in these activities to implement this particular order by the Presidency. Can we please go to page 3 now, and in the English -- Your Honours, could we please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D302. For the record, this is a criminal report by the Security Administration, dated the 21st of November, 1993. It was submitted to the district military prosecutor in Sarajevo. As I said, this is a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you please look at the preamble. You will agree that the criminal report was filed in keeping with the powers enshrined in the decree on district military courts and also in keeping with the Criminal Procedure Code that was adopted as the law of the Republic. You see that the person involved is Senad Hasic. And you know, don't you, that after these events in October 1993, so after these armed clashes, the showdown with those units, there were criminal reports being filed against dozens of perpetrators for all sorts of various crimes, including war crimes; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, can we please look at the last page so that the witness can see the signature. In the English as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will agree that the criminal report was signed by Chief Jusuf Jasarevic; right? Do you recognise the signature?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise the signature, and this is most probably General Jusuf Jasarevic's signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look further up, please, the penultimate paragraph. You will agree that those being reported committed crimes against humanity and international law as defined by Article 142 of the Criminal Code of the SFRY; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before we do that, I'm concerned that the B/C/S of this document has a lot of writing which is missing in the English. I want to understand why. I think it's a very important document, and we need to get all that is said. It's only two pages, but this last page of the B/C/S, for instance, as you can see, has got several paragraphs, and we've got only this one paragraph. And the first page is also -- in the English, we only have the names of the people, and in the B/C/S we have a lot said about each one of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we did submit this document for translation, but you know what sort of problems the Translation Unit is dealing with. At any rate, we can tell the Translation Unit that the Chamber has requested a full translation. I always ask for that, but they're simply buried in work, so they do what they can. So I will submit this document for admission, with the proviso that we shall be requesting a full translation. As for the bits that were added in hand, I see that I don't see the same thing in English, and I'm not sure what you mean. Can you please draw my attention to the relevant portions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic, this is page 16 of the English, just this -- I'm sorry. It's just this one paragraph on this page, and this is the page on which the author signed. But you can see that there are other page -- on the B/C/S, it's full, and if you go back to the previous pages, I'll show, too. Just a second --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- I just want to draw your attention to what I'm saying. I just want the full document translated. Can we go to the previous pages of both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand now, Your Honour. Yes, indeed. I understand. It's the translation problem that we have. I will do it, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I will ask that you get it translated fully. I understand they may be buried in work. If this -- I don't think this will bury them any deeper. It's a very small document. May -- the document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 960.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness D303. Page 2 of the document in the Bosnian, page 3 in the English. The English is fine; the Bosnian is not. We need page 2, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a report on status following investigation in the criminal case against Hasic, Senad. And if we could just lower the document slightly. Thank you. You see that it is signed by the deputy district military prosecutor, Hikmet Arnautovic, but can you please look at the first bullet, because these are activities that were implemented by the Security Administration. There is a report here on 61 persons from the former 9th Motorised Brigade and the former 10th Mountain Brigade against whom charges were pressed before the Military Court in Sarajevo. Could you just please have a look. Let's not waste any more time than necessary. I will quote to you the final part of this paragraph. It talks about the armed rebellion, armed uprising. That's about six lines down. And then it says against Topalovic, Armin Hodzic, Sarmin [phoen], Zija Kubat, [indiscernible]. All these names are given for the crime of war crime against civilians under Article 142, paragraph 1, of the adopted KZ of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Can I just be shown the relevant portion, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please just zoom in on the portion that I read out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. All right, I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the type of work that you did, you know that investigations that were conducted within the Military Security Department normally resulted in charges being pressed; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this case, this included war crimes against civilians; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if this document can be admitted and given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 961.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown Exhibit 241, please.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, until the document is shown on the screen, I would just like to ask you: You know that there was an action named "Trebevic-3" that was carried out, and you also participated in those activities; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document. It's a document of the Security Administration of the 6th of December, 1993, sent to the chiefs of the Military Security Services of all the Corps. It's entitled: "Engagement of the Military Security Service in the implementation of Operation Trebevic-3", and the document seeks reports or requests the reports. Can you please look at the part of this document where it says: "Reference". Do you see that? And you would agree that it refers to the order of the chief of the Security Administration of the 22nd of November, 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: From the text that I can read, yes, that's how -- that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please look at the text itself now. It's not long. If you can read it for yourself, please.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The order specifies the tasks of the Corps military security sectors to implement measures from the jurisdiction of the military police and in order to prevent crime and the obstruction of command and control; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, this is what I understand the text to say, yes, that reports are being asked for from the sectors of the Military Security Service that are subordinated to the Corps who have not already done so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to ask you the following: It's correct, isn't it, that the actual engagement of the Military Security Service was something that was done pursuant to orders of its chief?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: From what I know, yes, that was part of his competence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The chief of the Military Security Service set out the tasks to the Corps military security services that are part of their purview and also the tasks of the military police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: If you permit me, I would just like to clarify. The main tasks were already laid down in the rules. All the other tasks, individual, specific tasks, were something that were monitored by the chief of the administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. I would like the witness now to look at Exhibit 658. We can put this document that is up now away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I believe it's under seal, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Can we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, you may proceed, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document that was shown to you today by the Prosecutor. This is a report or information by the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps of the 16th of September, 1995. You commented today about some parts of the document. You also looked at the document and commented on it during proofing before beginning your testimony, yesterday and the day before yesterday. And in the report for the preparation for that trial, provided to us by the Prosecutor, you said the following: "As far as prisoners of war are concerned, there was sectors or commissions at corps level that dealt with prisoners of war. That's where it all ended. I do not recall that anything was done at the state level in connection with that. It was the duty of the corps to guard prisoners of war and to ensure contacts with the other side." What you told the Prosecutor during proofing is correct, isn't it? First of all, did you tell the Prosecutor this? Let's clarify that first.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I would say that, in essence, I did, yes. The bulk of it, yes. But I would just like to clarify. When I said "at the state level," and I think I did explain that, I meant primarily the institutions of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. When I mentioned "the state level," that's what I meant, the level of the General Staff or the Supreme Command Staff. And what I can recall of similar segments that dealt with these matters, other than the segment in the Security Administration, there were no such segments. So let me conclude. Prisoners of war -- there were no other segments that dealt with that matter at the level of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When we're talking about prisoners of war, from the time that they were captured until they were exchanged, it was all dealt with in lower units, up to corps level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, including the Corps. Yes, it ended at corps level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you talked about information received in this instance about prisoners of war through intercepted telefax messages, you said that this information had to be checked. Actually, what you said was this: "The 3rd Corps was supposed to check this information without asking me or needing me to tell them that the information needed to be checked." You also said --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's just to me it is not exactly clear, all the words which are going in right now, whether they come from the proofing note, whether it refers to this morning's testimony of the witness. We are basically here having a viva voce witness, and now at this point in time we are getting a lot of new evidence in which is not on the table, in the sense that, I mean, either you wish to use the proofing note, put it on ELMO so that the Judges can also see what it is about, or -- I don't think this witness has this morning talked in that great detail about POWs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I thought you understood, Madam Vidovic, and I thought maybe this is something that is between the two teams, because she said, at page 42, line 1 or 2: "And in the report for the preparation for that trial provided to us by the Prosecutor, you said the following." So it looks like there is some report that was undertaken in preparation for a trial and that the Prosecution gave it to the Defence. We don't have -- I don't have it, definitely. I don't know whether Judge Lattanzi has it. Yes, you are right, we are lost, but I thought you were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand, to a certain extent. I'm just saying it would be nice if the witness is asked today in general about the fact POW -- about POWs and so on, and based on what he says today, that questions can be put to him. What is happening since about two, three minutes is that certain portions which were said one, two or three days ago are read to the witness and are just going in as if he would have testified today, which is not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I heard about that, too. Madam Vidovic, we are indeed lost, at least the Bench is definitely lost. I thought your colleague was not. Now he says he's also lost. Can you help us? What are you reading from?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, possibly it's a question of interpretation. I was very clear when I said that I am talking about the proofing notes that we received from the Prosecutor, and the Prosecutor knows very well what I'm talking about. The problem is -- why I am not putting that on the ELMO is that we only received the Bosnian version of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And the problem is that the Chamber doesn't have a copy of the proofing notes, and --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believed, Your Honours, that the Prosecutor gave it to the Trial Chamber at the same time as they handed it over to the Defence. But in principle, I would like to respond to the objection by the Prosecutor. Actually, it's about the following: We receive these proofing notes so that we can, during the testimony of the witness, put questions which are contained in the proofing notes, and possibly the witness did not testify on these matters during the examination-in-chief. That is the essence and the reason why the Defence is furnished with the proofing notes, and this is why I'm a little bit surprised or wonder at this objection from the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just say, there are two proofing notes which have been sent, and you didn't say so far which of the two proofing notes you were quoting from. And my point, again, is that this witness, this morning, hasn't repeated the text which you read out to him. I mean, my suggestion would simply be: Ask him first about the document and the issues you wish to have from the witness, and then, based on his answer, put the questions to him. What you have done, you have just read out a proofing note without telling us which one of the two it is, and then have followed up from there, but maybe this witness, this morning, says something different than he said in proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, Madam Vidovic, since I came to the ICTY, I have never received a proofing note, and I have not received this proofing note. I don't know whether Judge Lattanzi received it. So when a document is being used in court which we don't have and which is ultimately not tendered into evidence, I find it very difficult to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I can just clarify. The proofing notes have not been sent to the Judges, themselves. The practice of the OTP is that Mr. Thomas Pittman and Mr. Tillman Blumenstock are cc'd on the proofing notes which are sent to the other side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Not for the side of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have done this on one occasion where a late translation came in so that it reaches the Judges, but the practice of the OTP so far is to send it to the legal officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand. I'm not suggesting that the Judges must be given the proofing notes. I'm just stating a fact, that we have never seen proofing notes. And I'm not inclined to agree with documents that are used in court which are not being tendered and which we don't have sight of, because when we write the judgement, we can say somebody was reading something and we don't know what it was he was reading, and we don't know what weight to give to that document. And I hope that Madam Vidovic is listening.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes, I'm listening and I understand. Maybe we can deal with the situation by not referring to the proofing notes at all. I mean, it is signed, but to cut everything short, because we're losing a lot of time in this discussion. I'm just going to ask the witness without further reference to the proofing notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what I would like to ask you is the following, please: It's correct, isn't it, that the 3rd Corps should have and it was its assignment to carry out checks about information that referred to prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: That segment, speaking specifically about the 3rd Corps that dealt with prisoners of war, I'm not sure about the exact establishment name of that segment in the 3rd Corps, but it was entrusted with prisoners of war. It was their duty, as part of their general work, to carry out that kind of work together in cooperation with other organs and services of the 3rd Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So without issuing any kind of specific order, the standard procedure was to check information received through listening in or interception, and this information had to be confirmed as well; am I correct?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: If I can give an explanation here. In this specific document, from what I can see, we have actually a document that consists of two parts. The first part is the introduction by the organ of the 3rd Corps Military Security Service. And then additionally, I can see that they're also attaching the information that the Military Security Service acquired by intercepting telephone calls from a certain group or by persons that they considered to be of interest. Information that is received, and I'm speaking in principle now, information that is received in this way by intercepting telephone conversations and listening in and tapping and recording, should have been checked. That was the duty of the Military Security Service. It was not acceptable to use raw data in further external reporting and for further external needs and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you said it was the duty of the Military Security Service organs in the last sentence, please, which security organ did you have in mind? Can you please clarify that.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Specifically, the establishment name of that organ was "the Department of the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps," from what I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away. I would now like to ask you about a fact that you mentioned this morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that as part of the Counter-Intelligence Affairs Department there was a sector for war crimes, and I just wanted us to clarify that. I would like you to explain to the Trial Chamber exactly what that was. In fact, that sector was established after The Hague Tribunal Prosecutor's visit in September 1994, and after the signing of a contract by the Government of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina with the international prosecutor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we stop here? Could we move into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Prosecutor, for keeping track of these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: For the record, P02096 is Exhibit 700.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And we are now in open session, Mr. Registrar?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Exhibit ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number 700.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just for the record, this is a proposal to introduce the Operative Action Vranduk, dated the 13th of May, 19 -- Your Honours, it seems that the number is wrong. I may have misspoken, myself. It's P2069, not "96". The transcript says "2096", but it's P02069, which is a different document. For the record: "Proposal for the introduction of the Operative Action Vranduk." The date is the 13th of May, 1995. It was sent to Army General Rasim Delic at the Visoko GLOC.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, can you look at the document, please, and let me ask you briefly about the procedure for introducing these operative actions. The procedure was like this, wasn't it: The Military Security Department of the Corps would propose for an operative action to be introduced; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then the Security Administration, based on its powers from the rules governing the work of military security, requests authorisation to use special methods, for example, to tap certain lines, to eavesdrop, and to listen in to various conversations, and this authorisation must be granted by the chief of the Supreme Command Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, because only the commander was authorised or had the power to authorise to the Military Security Service the use of these secret methods.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The microphone is off, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The powers of the commander, regarding measures, came down to this: Authorising secret methods and means; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, secret methods and means that the military security used for their work, introducing an operative action or an operative investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Using these sorts of methods and means; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It's true, isn't it, that the administration would normally state the reasons for which it believed that it was necessary to introduce such measures or this specific action; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I don't mean to waste your time, but I would link up this introduction of this operative action with the documents that I was looking at a while ago, and particularly the document in which I address Nedime in writing. Such information, among other things, indicated that one of the processing degrees should be introduced. For example, I ask the -- or request the army commander that he grant us the use of these secret methods of work so that we might be in a good situation to collect intelligence and to take certain measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this explanation, Witness. Can we please move on to this: You see that there are reasons stated here for which this operative action is introduced, and it says the way some Afro-Asian nationals arrived in the country of B and H, and then the way some of them display their religion or the way they practice their religion, and then the way the whole thing is financed, bankrolled, and the entire logistics support. And then if we can please move on to the next page. The English is all right. We need to move the Bosnian. Thank you. Please have a look, Witness. At the beginning of this text, it says: "Apart from the above mentioned as well as a number of other illegal actions and activities taken by some members of the detachment, what is also quite prominent is the issue of evading participation in combat activities." You agree that one of the reasons for introducing this action was allegedly, at least, this problem, the fact that the El Mujahid people were not participating in combat activities; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The El Mujahid Detachment were almost trying to weasel their way out of combat activities; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Talking about that particular body of foreigners, I would also like to mention members of Afro-Asian descent. Sorry, what we found of particular interest were persons from that group, those who very often turned up in various humanitarian organisations or worked for various humanitarian organisations and yet they passed themselves off as army members, which left us greatly confused. That much is certain. And we weren't sure what sort of approach to take vis-a-vis those people, in terms of our powers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you for that comprehensive and extensive clarification, Witness. Let's look at the signature, please. What the Security Administration is proposing here, this is something that General Delic approved; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Can I please look at the final portion of the document?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Final portion, please, page 3. In the English, it's the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, he approved it, and I know that for a fact, that he did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this exhibit please be given a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 964.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put this document away now. Thank you. Can we now please have P2072. For the record, this is from the Military Security Service Administration, the 13th of May, 1995. The document is entitled: "Preparation for the implementation of Vranduk operative action," sent to the 3rd and 7th Corps Commands, this assignment, Military Security Department. It's a brief document. Witness, can you please read it to yourself first.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you look at the last paragraph, please. It reads: "Coordinating groups, including members of the SVB and RBH MUP, State Security Service Administration, shall be dispatched to your Corps zone of responsibility so that they can help with planning the implementation of the Vranduk operation." Right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I agree that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Do you agree that the Security Administration of the Supreme Command Staff did not stop at a formal order; it continued to pursue specific activities and to send their own teams to help with work in the field; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes. You can see, based on this, that there was a continuity to the implementation of the order signed by General Delic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be given an exhibit number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 965.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, maybe we can move into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, as you see, this is Special Information number 12, the 2nd of April, 1993. Can we please look at page 2. It reads: "Information on inappropriate behaviour of Rasim Delic." Can you please look at the portion which says -- it's midway down the large paragraph, the second paragraph. It reads: "Among the fighters and the officers, as well as among the inhabitants of Visoko, Delic lost respect, since he was acting like a conformist, disinterested in combat activity, spending his time very often in bars and hotels and so on and so forth." Can we please go to the bottom of the page. Witness, Fikret Muslimovic, the person who signed this, is this the same person as General Muslimovic, the person you mentioned meeting?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, and I recognise his signature.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you agree with this description that was provided here of Rasim Delic as a person? You knew him. You worked there, after all, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: In the briefest possible terms, no. If you grant me more time, I could also state my opinion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Can you offer a brief opinion, please? We don't have that much time.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Those who wanted the best for all the ethnic groups in Bosnia and Herzegovina were people for whom he set an example, and he set the guidelines in his public appearances for future development for Bosnia and Herzegovina. I know at least three persons who, because of his views and positions, although they belonged to different ethnic groups, were not Muslims, decided to remain in the Military Security Administration, because he was a subtle person, because his methods were subtle, and this was very much in demand in the sector of the General Staff. I'm talking about the views of General Rasim Delic, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. Let me ask you something else in relation to Fikret Muslimovic. After he left the Military Security Service in 1994, he became an adviser to President Izetbegovic; am I right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: As far as I know, after he left the Military Security Service he became an adviser to President Izetbegovic, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then after that, in 1995, the Presidency appointed him as head of the Morale Administration; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I think it was roughly around that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please put this document away now. Exhibit 666, under seal, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: In private session? Do you want to go in private session, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies, Your Honours. That's what I have, but all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it's under seal, Madam Vidovic, so we don't need to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No need. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: For the record, the Chamber is in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and my apologies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, briefly, this is a document, report produced by the Military Security Service Administration, dated the 21st of June, 1995, or the Security Service Department. What I want to know is, do you recognise this handwriting here?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Which one do you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My apologies. Witness, allow me to explain. I'm talking about the upper right corner here of this document. You see that there's a handwritten note there; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Where it says "01"?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What it says right there: "Keep in mind that information to do with this unit should not be used outside the service," that's what the note says, is the handwriting familiar?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, it's quite familiar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So whose is it?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Sacir Arnautovic, I suppose. I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness. Sacir Arnautovic, Sacir Arnautovic? Can we just see the date, please. The 21st of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly was Sacir Arnautovic doing at the time?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I think he was deputy head of the Security Administration at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please put this document away. Exhibit 784 is my next document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, this is a document of the 3rd Corps Security Service Department. The date is the 22nd of June, 1995. Could this document please be displayed in such a way that the witness can look at the handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us whose handwriting this appears to be? Is that the same handwriting as before? (redacted) It's the same handwriting, and I think this is Sacir Arnautovic's handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We can put this document away too. Just another document that I've been meaning to show the witness, PT2971B. Page 7, please, in the B/C/S, and page 2 in the English. For the record, this is a protocol of the General Staff of the BH Army, Security Administration, between the 1st of October, 1995, and the 31st of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, please look at these tables. That's right. Do you agree that at the top of the page -- or, rather, can we just focus on the document in such a way as to enlarge the part of the page where we can actually see what the columns are in reference to. Thank you. A little more, please. Thank you. The first column, it says: "Original number," and then "Transfer," and then it says: "Subject".

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, you agree that this is a book where incoming mail was recorded and filed under a certain number?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, this was supposed to be the register that was kept by people in charge of general affairs, but I can't really tell you how many times I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. There's one thing that I wish to ask you. Look at these cells up here. It says: "Centre" and so on.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: I see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm trying to ask you this: You see exactly who sent a certain document to the Security Administration; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, it's perfectly visible, based on what I'm looking at, it's clear as day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you perhaps help us with this? It says: "Organisational Unit"?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then it says: "Sign" or "Distribute"?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that the document was then distributed and sent to another address, sent on; is that what it means?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, that was the understanding, and as far as I can tell, based on what I can read underneath this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I take us slowly through? We are lost, Madam Vidovic. I'm not quite sure what you are talking about. All right? Now, how does one, by looking at those columns, determine -- that means that the document was then distributed and sent to another address?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, how shall I put it? It's the second table in the English. The last column is "Distribution on." Do you see that? Oh, that one, yes. Can we just look at something specific to clarify this. In the Bosnian, from table 3, from the top of the page down. That's table 2 on our screens now in the English.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, it says: "Results of interviews, Gojic, Mile, and Banjac, Nebojsa." You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: No, I don't. Could you please zoom in a little?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, that's right, like that, like that. Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's good.

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: This is the third horizontal line; right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've seen that?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you agree that the document has a number, and then it reads "Sender," name and place, and then over there, if we could please scroll to the right -- I don't have that much time -- where it says "Distributed to," we can see that on the 16th of October this document was sent to the MUP and to the SDB, State Security Service; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. There are two references to that, as a matter of fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Based on this register or the book of protocols, we can always ascertain whether a document was received by the Military Security Administration in Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, that's what these books were used for. I fully agree.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. We can also plot the movements of a particular document and which part of the Security Administration was processing a certain document; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes. If you look at the numbers, you should be able to see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you can see the final destiny of a certain document, where it was eventually processed, where it went for final processing, in the last column; right?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, where it says "Sign" or "Mark," column 9, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because right above, it says "Distributed to," so we can see a list of addressees there and we see who the document was sent to?

utterances.speaker: PW-13
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly on the money.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, thank you. I have no further questions for this witness, and I would like a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 968.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Neuner, re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge. Just one question, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: At page 49, line 5, I interrupted you when you were answering your question. I would like you to finish that sentence. You were saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, that brings us to the conclusion of your testimony. Let me take this time to say thank you very much to you for coming to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please travel well back home. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may briefly address you to thank you, and I do sincerely hope that you found my evidence helpful. All of this is for the sake of finding out the truth about what happened in my country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I almost called your name, sorry. But just wait there until the blinds are down. Don't move yet. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The matter then stands adjourned to tomorrow at quarter past 2.00 in the afternoon in Courtroom III. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 7th day of December, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 24

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
